supersessionReason: Pre-implementation review found that v5 did not distinguish an evidence-verification failure from an atomic pointer-batch failure after successful evidence verification.

evidenceVerificationFailure.meaning: committed response or sidecar bytes, hashes, identity, or semantic binding did not verify
evidenceVerificationFailure.retry: may only converge on the immutable failure or fail verification again; it may not rewrite the object, manifest, sidecar, or pointer

pointerBatchFailureAfterSuccessfulVerifi.meaning: both committed-row R2 objects verified, but the atomic verification-event and pointer batch failed or returned an unknown result
retry: read the committed manifest and extension
re-read and verify both R2 objects and all hashes
converge on the deterministic capture-derived publication event token
advance the pointer forward only in the same batch as that event
pointerBatchFailureAfterSuccessfulVerifi.immutableFailureHistory: preserve any prior pointer-publication failure event and alert
pointerBatchFailureAfterSuccessfulVerifi.heartbeatRecovery: a later successful verification may restore current only when its verification time is not older than the latest recorded attempt

manifestBatchFailure.candidateEligibility: none until a later invocation commits the complete atomic manifest-candidate batch

attemptIdentityCorrection.verifiedPublicationEvent: deterministic token derived from contract version, captureId, and verified-publication phase so all workers converge
attemptIdentityCorrection.postManifestFailureEvent: deterministic distinct token derived from original attempt, captureId, and failed phase

freshnessBinding.startupValidation: every profile threshold must equal its named operating-contract value or frozen minimum

effectiveContract: source-capture-contract.2026.1 plus v2, v3 except its superseded same-batch pointer clause, v4 except its superseded manifest-time verification clause, v5, and every clarification in this file
